title: For q>p and noncoalescing positive-real-part paired parameters satisfying (1.13), the complex-field Barnes–Ismagilov integral equals the finite quadratic hypergeometric expression Sigma_+^C
difficulty: The central obligation is to evaluate an integral with a simultaneous discrete Mellin index and continuous contour variable, whose paired Gamma poles must be matched across both indices. The proof derives their joint lattice parametrization, computes complex Gamma residues and reorganizes them into a finite sum of products of ordinary hypergeometric series with a convergence justification. This exceeds a routine single-variable residue exercise and does not merely apply the classical Meijer formula without the new discrete-index calculation.

title: For q>1 and c>0, the nonstandard quantum complex projective-line C*-algebra is the pullback of two Toeplitz algebras along their common symbol map
difficulty: The substantive obligation is to recover the entire quantum homogeneous-space algebra from its concrete operator family, rather than identify a quotient or only a fixed representation. The author constructs two separate compact-operator ideals from defect projections, derives the double weighted-shift decomposition and controls the possible unitary remainder by its invariant spectrum. A final parameter-removing change of basis completes the faithful pullback realization; this is beyond standard qualifying operator theory.
